findings.title: [P1] Retain tenant scoping in document lookups
findings.body: When document IDs are tenant-local or user-controlled, querying only by `documentId` allows `getDocument` to return another tenant's matching record. The previous query included `tenantId`, and the service still receives `ctx.tenantId`; retain that constraint to preserve tenant isolation.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported cache module contract
findings.body: Deleting `src/cache.ts` removes the exported `readCached` entry point entirely, so existing direct consumers can no longer resolve the module or symbol. If this API is being retired, provide a compatible migration path rather than removing it while claiming existing contracts are preserved.

findings.title: [P1] Retain tenant scoping in document lookups
findings.body:
Any request using a database containing tenant-local document IDs now queries only by `documentId`. If two tenants share an ID—or a caller supplies another tenant’s ID—`getDocument` can return data outside `ctx.tenantId`, causing cross-tenant disclosure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore the exported cache module
findings.body:
Existing consumers importing `src/cache` or `readCached` can no longer resolve the module, producing a compile-time/module-resolution failure rather than preserving the exported API contract.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping to document lookups
findings.body:
In a shared multi-tenant database, an authenticated user who supplies a document ID belonging to another tenant can retrieve that tenant’s document because the query no longer includes `ctx.tenantId`. This is a cross-tenant authorization bypass and data disclosure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
